solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Percy would repeat what reivers did

indicators.note: to repeat something is to say it again, so the contraction is spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: Henry Percy, Shakespeare's Hotspur, was called Harry, so 'Percy would' is 'Harry would', contracted to Harry'd

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark that someone called Percy would echo the deeds of old raiders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeat' signals that 'Harry'd' is said aloud. Reivers were the raiders of the Anglo-Scottish Borders, where the Percys were a leading family.
explanation.definitionFit: Reivers raided and plundered, which is to harass or lay waste, the past tense matching 'did'.

clue.text: A shock's thrown 15

indicators.note: something thrown is tossed about and lands jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of 'A shock's', including the S of the possessive, are the fodder

explanation.surface: A shock has floored the person at 15, like a blow knocking someone to their knees.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 15 across, KNEELER.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm cushion for kneeling on in church is called both a hassock and a kneeler.

clue.text: Protein I rescue can be cooked if you accept recipe for it

definitions.text: Protein I rescue can be cooked if you accept recipe for it

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe (from Latin 'recipe', take), as on old prescriptions

indicators.note: cooking changes how ingredients are arranged, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A cook explains that leftover meat can be saved if you follow a recipe for this dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If you accept' tells you to add R (recipe) to the letters of PROTEIN I RESCUE before rearranging. The whole clue also describes the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A resurrection pie is made from leftovers, so it rescues protein that might be thrown away; the clue describes its purpose.

clue.text: Couple killing time

indicators.note: killing breaks something apart, so the letters of 'time' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two people idly killing time together.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people in a romantic relationship are called an item, an informal idiom for a pair.

clue.text: Giant allowing early start on Sunday to couple after dungeon's opening

indicators.note: after means everything else follows the dungeon's opening letter
a dungeon's opening is the first letter of the word dungeon
the start of the word early is its opening letter, as an early start is a beginning

parts.note: a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: A giant lets his prisoners out early on Sunday to pair up after the dungeon door opens.
explanation.walkthrough: Giant Despair is the ogre of Doubting Castle in Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress, who throws Christian and Hopeful into his dungeon.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Pilgrim's Progress the giant who imprisons the pilgrims is named Despair.

clue.text: Dark brown or light brown will restrict artist

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: camel is a light yellowish-brown colour, like the animal's coat
RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A colour chart choice between dark and light browns that limits a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Caramel names a deep brown shade, the colour of burnt sugar.

clue.text: Charlie: name after doing wrong that's well-deserved

indicators.note: after means the abbreviation for name follows the jumbled letters

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: doing something wrong muddles it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Charlie earns a name for misbehaving, and the punishment that follows is just.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing wrong' reads as misbehaviour; 'wrong' alone rearranges DOING into ONDIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Condign is used of punishment that fits the offence, meaning fully merited.

clue.text: Part of Belorussia facing north

indicators.note: in a down entry, facing north means the letters are read upwards, back to front
of points to letters drawn from inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A region of Belarus that looks northward.
explanation.walkthrough: Belorussia is the older name for Belarus; take ELOR from its start and read it bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A part in a play or project is the role someone takes, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Erroneous understanding paper is ordered for woman in embassy

indicators.note: in places the jumbled paper and woman inside the word for embassy

parts.note: a mission is a diplomatic embassy abroad

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters of 'paper' are rearranged

parts.note: hen is an informal word for a woman, especially in Scotland

explanation.surface: A diplomatic mix-up: someone has ordered the wrong paper for a woman working at an embassy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hen' for a woman is chiefly Scottish and northern English; 'in' asks for the embassy word to be split open.
explanation.definitionFit: A misapprehension is a mistaken belief, a false grasp of the facts.

clue.text: Southern lake is preferred to aquarium first used in ceremonial purification

indicators.note: one letter is chosen over another, so it replaces it

parts.note: austral means southern, as in Australia or aurora australis

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of aquarium

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A southern lake is chosen over a fish tank as the first water for a purifying rite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is preferred to' swaps A (aquarium first) for L (lake) in AUSTRAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustral describes water or rites used for ritual cleansing, from Latin lustrum, a purification.

clue.text: Dismantled New York masts easily in two seconds for review of computer operations

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters between the two letters for seconds

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second, and two of them give S and S

indicators.note: dismantled things are taken apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ships' masts in New York are taken down easily in a couple of seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In two seconds' sounds like a time limit, but it is the S at each end that holds the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Systems analysis is the study of how a computer setup works, to improve it.

clue.text: Ring with keeper on either side on a lady's fingers

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: the letters on either side of keeper are its first and last

explanation.surface: A ring, worn with a guard ring, sits on a woman's fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: A keeper is also a ring worn to stop another slipping off, which makes the surface hang together.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra pods are commonly known as ladies' fingers from their slim tapering shape.

clue.text: For well-managed après-ski with bit of entertainment seek out a Hilton …

indicators.note: managing something well rearranges it into good order, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters of après-ski, without its accent and hyphen

indicators.note: a bit of entertainment is its first letter

parts.note: the letters of seek are taken out of the pool, as 'out' signals

explanation.surface: A tip for a smooth evening after skiing: find a hotel with some entertainment laid on.
explanation.walkthrough: Pool APRES-SKI with E, remove the letters of SEEK ('seek out'), and rearrange what is left. The Hilton is a person, not the hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris Hilton is a celebrity heiress, so a Hilton is one member of that family.

clue.text: … losing one second opening box

indicators.note: opening means the letter for second moves to the front
losing means the letter for one is dropped

parts.note: the dots carry over the answer to the clue before, the city name
one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: The Hilton, having lost a second, starts to spar.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots carry on from 11 across, so the previous answer is the material here.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box, especially in practice bouts.

clue.text: Find fault with cripple brought to book …

indicators.note: brought to means the word for cripple comes up against the letter for book

parts.note: to lame someone is to cripple them

explanation.surface: A disabled person is criticised and held to account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought to book' is an idiom for being called to account, which makes the surface read naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: To blame is to hold responsible, censuring someone for a failing.

clue.text: … being enabled to walk

indicators.note: being enabled means being set up differently, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the dots carry over the answer to the clue before, the word for find fault

explanation.surface: Continuing 13: the lame person is now able to walk.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots carry on from 13 down, whose answer is the material rearranged here.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at an easy, leisurely pace.

clue.text: One being dubbed knight in ship by the Queen?

indicators.note: in puts the chess piece inside the word for ship

parts.note: the keel is the ship's backbone, here standing for the whole vessel
N is the knight in chess notation
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A knight is dubbed aboard ship by the Queen, perhaps like Drake.
explanation.walkthrough: Being dubbed a knight, one kneels before the monarch, so the definition is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone receiving a knighthood kneels to be touched on the shoulder with a sword.

clue.text: Variously L, M and N are initially used of number

indicators.note: variously means in different ways, so the letters are rearranged
initially picks the first letter of used

explanation.surface: A note that the letters L, M and N appear in various numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: L and M are themselves Roman numerals, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, numeral means relating to or expressing a figure.

clue.text: Player disqualification includes four in Test Match corrupted after first two are dismissed

indicators.note: includes means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a ban is a disqualification from taking part

indicators.note: corrupted means altered, so these letters are rearranged
only four letters are kept in play, so everything past them is dropped
the opening pair of letters of the cricket phrase is sent away like two batters out

parts.note: the letters of Test Match are the source

explanation.surface: A player banned for match-fixing in a Test, after two others were sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four in' means keep only four letters once the first two are gone, so the tail of 'match' goes too; a contrived but fair cricket-flavoured device.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman is a cricket player whose job is to bat.

clue.text: Not as high as peak heat waves

parts.note: a ben is a Scottish mountain peak, as in Ben Nevis

indicators.note: heat waves suggests the letters shimmer and shift, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Heat waves rise from a mountain top, below its summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heat waves' looks like one phrase but 'waves' is a verb rearranging HEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Beneath means below or under, so lower than something.

clue.text: Hacking this list to bits I could be making a subtle distinction

definitions.text: Hacking this list to bits I could be making a subtle distinction

indicators.note: hacking chops things up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: these letters, together with the answer ('this'), make up the letters of 'a subtle distinction'

explanation.surface: Someone muses that tearing this list apart would draw a fine distinction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' stands for the answer: the answer plus LIST TO BITS I, hacked up, gives A SUBTLE DISTINCTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuanced describes something that draws fine shades of meaning.

clue.text: Sporting occasion entertained one noted for integrity

parts.note: a gala is a sporting event, such as a swimming gala
had, as in had guests over, means entertained

explanation.surface: A sports event hosted someone known for honesty.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad, the purest Arthurian knight, is a byword for virtue.

clue.text: Part of Glasgow not socially acceptable Labour's redeveloped

definitions.text: Part of Glasgow not socially acceptable Labour's redeveloped

indicators.note: part of picks the first letter of Glasgow
redeveloped means rebuilt in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged
not means the letter for socially acceptable is dropped

parts.note: the letters of Labour's, with the S of the possessive
U means upper-class, socially acceptable, from the old U and non-U labels

explanation.surface: A rough district of Glasgow has been rebuilt by the Labour council.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' removes U ('socially acceptable') from LABOURS; 'redeveloped' rearranges what remains, after G.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gorbals is a district of Glasgow, once a notorious slum, later redeveloped.

clue.text: Work of art in Dutch church representing Pity

indicators.note: representing means presenting in another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Dutch church painting depicting compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Representing' looks like 'depicting' in the surface, but it is the signal to rearrange the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: A diptych is a painting on two hinged panels, often an altarpiece.

clue.text: Element. Gaseous one. Nitrogen

indicators.note: a gas has freely moving parts, so the letters of one are rearranged

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Like a chemistry textbook: an element, a gas, then nitrogen.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is a chemical element, one of the noble gases.

clue.text: Appropriately, 11 twos

indicators.note: appropriately suggests a rearrangement that fits the case

parts.note: 11 refers to the answer at 11 across, the French capital

explanation.surface: A cryptic note that the city at 11 suits pairs of things.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris suits couples, so the rearrangement is appropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: Pairs are sets of two, so 'twos' is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Photo cards

definitions.meaning: an informal photograph, a quick shot
a children's card game where matching cards are called out

explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a casual photo, and the children's card game is named for the call made on a match.

clue.text: About two-fifths of Aboriginal initiation rite

indicators.note: about means turned around, so those letters are rearranged
two-fifths of a ten-letter word is its first four letters

explanation.surface: Roughly two-fifths of Aboriginal people undergo a coming-of-age ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' rearranges ABOR, the first two-fifths of ABORIGINAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A bora is an Australian Aboriginal ceremony initiating boys into manhood.

clue.text: Italian dance's one-off performance

parts.note: a gig is a single musical performance
A means one

explanation.surface: An Italian dance is a single show.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'Italian dance is, one off, performance': taking A (one) off the answer leaves GIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Giga is the Italian form of the jig, a lively Baroque dance.

clue.text: Open quality: skill at getting ball on green?

parts.note: in golf, an approach shot is played to land the ball on the green
ability is skill or aptitude

explanation.surface: A golfer's skill at reaching the green, needed at the Open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' hints at golf's Open Championship, but it means friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being open and easy to talk to is approachability, a friendly quality.

clue.text: Scots green line had to be reviewed

indicators.note: reviewed means looked at again in another way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scottish green with a line needing another look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' means naive, not the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, Hieland (Highland) is used of someone naive or unsophisticated, inexperienced like a newcomer.

clue.text: Use styptic for cuts and cut out hospital

indicators.note: out means out of order, so these letters are rearranged
cut means the last letter of and is removed

explanation.surface: First aid: treat cuts with a styptic, and remove someone from hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' trims AND to AN; 'out' rearranges CUTS and AN to STAUNC. A styptic stops bleeding.
explanation.definitionFit: To staunch a wound is to stop its bleeding, which is what a styptic does.
